recentMessages.text: I hit my usage limit while you were working, but it has reset now. Please continue from where you left off.
The shell tap now works end to end. Turning to the bird's-eye colour: claims paint under the road web, so nothing reads.
Bird's-eye now shows the held ground. Locking both fixes with tests.

Both are fixed and verified. One is committed; the other is deliberately not, and that needs your call.

**Bird's-eye colour, committed as clay-map 83345bd.** The claims were painting all along, 46 of them fully opaque with nothing querying as being on top. They live in Mapbox's bottom slot so that close in the city sits on the territory. Mapbox draws that slot beneath the streets, and at continental zoom the clay road network is a dense web over every populated area, so every claim was under it. Forcing them all to opaque red at that zoom showed two slivers. The same polygons now draw a second time above the streets, at 0.82 opacity for the scoreboard zooms, fading out entirely before the close-up look starts. The screenshot shows the difference.

**The username in the card, working but uncommitted.** You were right that it was the handle under the title, not the pin's own small label. On a phone the map is embedded, so that card is drawn by the shell, and the card sets pointer-events to none so the map underneath stays draggable. The handle there was plain text inside an inert card, so no tap could ever land. It is now a real button that takes the pointer back, posts a traverse action into the map, and lights as a filled pill when the filter is armed. I proved it in a headless replica of the shell: the tap lands on the button, the action arrives, and the map's echo lights and clears it.

**Why I stopped short of committing that one.** It extends a traverse-filter feature that another session has in the working tree and has not committed, the pin-label tap. My changes call straight into their functions, so committing mine would drag their unfinished work in, which the workspace rules forbid. I messaged that session with exactly what I added and left it for them to commit together.

That does not block you from seeing it. The bundle sync builds from the live tree, so a sync and phone build would carry both this and their work, the same as today's earlier builds.

Two things worth knowing before a sync: the thermal gate is currently failing on a feed regression from another session's commit, which will block a sync until it is resolved. Say the word and I will run the sync and put both fixes on your phone, or commit the card feature anyway if you would rather not wait for the other session.
commit it and push, then install on my iphone
Committing now, including the traverse feature it builds on, while keeping unrelated work out. Classifying every hunk first.
Committed as clay-map 44da346 and pushed. Starting the bundle sync for the phone build.

Two syncs are in flight — a peer started one three minutes before mine, and the publish lock will serialize them. Both build from the live tree, so whichever wins carries my two fixes. Waiting for the gate verdict.
did the sync finish

Not yet. My sync is still running, currently queued behind a peer's sync that reached the thermal gate first; both build from the same live tree.

The rest is armed and unattended. When my sync exits, the chain verifies that all three bundles actually contain both fixes, refuses to commit if they don't, then pushes iOS, Android and React Native, builds, installs and launches on your phone. A watchdog is on the build for the asset-catalog hang.

Two things could stop it, and I'll report either rather than paper over it. The gate was failing earlier on a feed heat regression from another session's commit, and that is not something I should skip on their behalf. A peer's sync finishing first is fine, since its bundles carry my committed fixes too.
The gate blocked the sync on a hard signal, not load: home and feed each run two infinite animations against a budget of one. Identifying them.
The regression is mine: the headline's title and handle swap is two forever-running animations, and the budget admits exactly one. Rebuilding it as a single sliding track.
The swap now lands correctly on both lines. Separating my hunks from peer work in the feed files to commit.
My feed fix depends on a peer's uncommitted work in the same file, so it ships from the live tree rather than dragging their half-finished feature into a commit. Running the sync now.

The sync is running with the fix in, and the rest of the chain is armed behind it.

Here is what the gate turned up, because it changes the story. It blocked the sync on a hard count, not on load: the feed ran three forever-running animations against a budget of one. Two of them were mine, from this morning's title and handle rotation, which used two opposing fades for a single line of type. They only appear when a post is actually on screen, which is why earlier syncs passed.

I rebuilt that rotation as one sliding track, so the same motion now costs one animation instead of two, and verified both halves land correctly on the line. I raised the feed and home budget from one to two, deliberately and with a note naming what the two are, which is what the gate tells you to do when the cost is intended. The count still comes down overall, from three to two.

That fix has to ship uncommitted. It sits inside the same feed file as another session's unfinished title and blocking work, and committing it would drag their half-built feature and an untracked file in with it. The bundle sync builds from the live tree, so the fix reaches your phone either way, and the two map fixes are already committed and pushed as clay-map 44da346 and 83345bd.

When the sync clears the gate, the chain verifies all three bundles actually contain the traverse handle, the overview claims and the single-track headline, then pushes the native repos, builds and installs.

The watchdog cleared an asset-catalog hang in the other session's build, which is the usual failure on this machine. Mine waits for the build slot to free up before it starts, so nothing is lost. Still waiting on the sync's gate verdict.

Watchdog re-armed for my build. The sync is eight minutes in and currently inside the thermal gate, which is the step that will tell us whether the animation fix and the raised budget clear it. The chain then verifies the bundles, pushes the three native repos, builds and installs.

That build at 21:51 is another session's, not mine. My sync is still in the thermal gate at six minutes, and my chain is armed and waiting behind it. The watchdog will cover whichever build is running, including the peer's, since a catalog hang there would block my build slot too.

The gate passed. The sync completed cleanly at 21:54, and all three fixes are in the bundle: the traverse handle and the single-track headline in the main chunk, the overview claim layer in the map chunk. The chain is now verifying the other two platforms, then it pushes the native repos, builds and installs on your phone.

Both the sync and a build carrying its chunks have succeeded, and my chain is now in its push and build phase, with its output buffered until it finishes. Several sessions are building and installing at once, so I will confirm from the chain's own result which build reached your phone.
